# obol.cluster

:::caution[v3 release candidate, unreleased]

This is the reference for `@obolnetwork/obol-sdk@3.0.0-rc.12`, generated from its source and spec. Names and shapes may still change before 3.0.0, and it is not on npm `latest`. For the released SDK see the [2.x reference](../../sdk/index.md).

:::

Cluster definitions and locks: build and post a definition, accept it as an operator, follow it until the lock is published, and verify definitions and locks (hashes, EIP-712 and EIP-1271 signatures, BLS share binding and deposit signatures) without running Charon. The verifiers also work without a client, from the `cluster` namespace.

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: cluster.prepareDefinition</summary>

Tag: `pure`. Builds an unsigned definition and its config hash; nothing is signed or sent.

Inputs:

```
{ name: string, operators: { address: Address }[], validators: { feeRecipientAddress: Address, withdrawalAddress: Address }[],
  depositAmounts: bigint[]?, compounding: bool? (false), targetGasLimit: uint? (200000000),
  consensusProtocol: "" | "qbft" ? (""), version: string? ("v1.11.0"),
  creator: Address, chainId: uint, uuid: string?, timestamp: string? }   # uuid / timestamp generated when absent
```

Checks:

1. `version` is v1.10.0 or later (`v1.10.0`, `v1.11.0`), else [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) (path `version`). Older versions sign less
   of the definition: they remain hashable and verifiable (`computeConfigHash`, `verifyLock`) for existing clusters, but
   are not created, and the Obol API rejects them for new clusters.
2. At least 4 operators; addresses valid, unique case-insensitively; either all set or all empty (solo / Charon
   flows). Else [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID). (2.15 `validateUniqueAddresses`)
3. At least 1 validator; fee recipient and withdrawal addresses non-zero. (2.15)
4. Each `depositAmounts` entry is whole gwei and one of 1, 32 ETH (or 1, 8, 32, 256 ETH with `compounding`). (2.15)
5. No unknown fields. (2.15 `additionalProperties: false`)

Output: `{ definition, configHash }` with `threshold = ceil(2n/3)` for n operators, `num_validators`, `fork_version`
of the chain, `dkg_algorithm: "default"`, `creator.address`, amounts written in gwei. (2.15)

</details>

<summary>Specification: cluster.create</summary>

Tag: `api` (+ wallet). Input: the output of `prepareDefinition` (or its input). Signs `CreatorConfigHash
{ creator_config_hash: configHash }` with the wallet and posts the definition.

Checks:

### cluster.accept {#accept}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">api (+ wallet)</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 2</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#create">3. Create and join the cluster</a></div>

Joins a cluster as an operator: fetches the definition, verifies it
(`verifyDefinition`, else DEFINITION_INVALID), checks the wallet account is one of its
operators (ACCOUNT_NOT_OPERATOR), then signs the config hash and the ENR and posts them.
Accepting again with the same ENR returns the definition without signing.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.cluster.accept(input: {
  configHash: string;
  enr: string;
  version?: string;
}): Promise<ClusterDefinition>
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>input</code> | <span class="sdk-type">{ configHash: string; enr: string; version?: string; }</span> |  |
| <code>input.configHash</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |
| <code>input.enr</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |
| <code>input.version?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">Promise&lt;<a href="./types/cluster#ClusterDefinition">ClusterDefinition</a>&gt;</span>

**Throws** <span class="sdk-muted">(per spec)</span> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--error" href="../errors#DEFINITION_INVALID">DEFINITION_INVALID</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--error" href="../errors#ACCOUNT_NOT_OPERATOR">ACCOUNT_NOT_OPERATOR</a> <span class="sdk-muted">plus the [checks every operation runs](../errors.md#checks-every-operation-runs)</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { cluster } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

// As an operator: verifies the definition, then signs it and your ENR.
const updated = await obol.cluster.accept({ configHash, enr });
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: cluster.accept</summary>

Tag: `api` (+ wallet). Inputs: `{ configHash: Hash32, enr: string }`.

Checks:

1. G3.
2. Fetch the definition (`GET /v1/definition/:configHash`) and run `verifyDefinition` with the client chain; any
   failure is [`DEFINITION_INVALID`](../errors.md#DEFINITION_INVALID). (2.15 `getVerifiedClusterDefinition`)
3. An explicit `version` in the input equals the definition's version, else [`DEFINITION_INVALID`](../errors.md#DEFINITION_INVALID). (2.15)
4. The definition's version is v1.10.0 or later, else [`DEFINITION_INVALID`](../errors.md#DEFINITION_INVALID) (`version_unsupported`): older versions
   sign less of the definition. (2.15)
5. The wallet account is one of `definition.operators[].address` (case-insensitive), else [`ACCOUNT_NOT_OPERATOR`](../errors.md#ACCOUNT_NOT_OPERATOR). (2.15)
6. If that operator already has a `config_signature` and the same ENR, return the definition without signing
   (idempotent). (2.15)

Then sign `OperatorConfigHash { operator_config_hash: configHash }` and `ENR { enr }` and
`PUT /v1/definition/:configHash` with the operator payload. Output: the updated definition.

Tag: `api`. `get(configHash)` → definition (`GET /v1/definition/:configHash`). `getLock({ configHash } | { lockHash })`
→ lock (`GET /v1/lock/configHash/:configHash` or `GET /v1/lock/:lockHash`). Check: the hash is 32-byte hex before it

### cluster.watch {#watch}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">api</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#create">3. Create and join the cluster</a></div>

Follows a definition until its lock is published: yields `operator_signed` once per
newly signed operator, `definition_ready` once, then `lock_published` and ends. Polls
every `intervalMs` (default 12 s) and backs off on rate limits; aborting `signal` ends
the iteration without an error.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.cluster.watch(
  configHash: string,
  options: WatchOptions,
): AsyncIterable<ClusterEvent>
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>configHash</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |
| <code>options</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/cluster#WatchOptions">WatchOptions</a></span> |  |
| <code>options.signal</code> | <span class="sdk-type">AbortSignal</span> |  |
| <code>options.intervalMs?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">number</span> | Poll interval in ms; default 12,000, minimum 2,000. |
| <code>options.sleep?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">(ms: number, signal: AbortSignal) =&gt; Promise&lt;void&gt;</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">AsyncIterable&lt;<a href="./types/cluster#ClusterEvent">ClusterEvent</a>&gt;</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { cluster } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const controller = new AbortController();
for await (const event of obol.cluster.watch(configHash, { signal: controller.signal })) {
  if (event.type === 'operator_signed') console.log(`${event.signed}/${event.total} signed`);
  if (event.type === 'lock_published') console.log('lock', event.lockHash); // the iterator ends here
}
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: cluster.watch</summary>

Tag: `api`. Inputs: `configHash: Hash32`, `{ signal: AbortSignal, intervalMs: uint? }`. Output: an async iterable of

```
{ type: "operator_signed", address: Address, signed: uint, total: uint }
{ type: "definition_ready" }
{ type: "lock_published", lockHash: Hash32 }
```

Rules: poll `GET /v1/definition/:configHash` until every operator has `config_signature` and `enr_signature`, emitting
`operator_signed` once per newly signed operator and `definition_ready` once; then poll
`GET /v1/lock/configHash/:configHash` (404 = not yet) until it returns, emit `lock_published` and end. A
`definition_ready` / `lock_published` that is already true on the first poll is still emitted. Abort ends the
iteration without an error. API errors other than 404 are thrown from the iterator. See
[`lifecycles.md`](https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/lifecycles.md#cluster).

Polling: every `intervalMs` (default 12,000, minimum 2,000); after an [`API_RATE_LIMIT`](../errors.md#API_RATE_LIMIT), [`API_TIMEOUT`](../errors.md#API_TIMEOUT) or 5xx it
doubles the wait up to 60,000 and returns to `intervalMs` after a success, and only throws after 5 failures in a row.
An API stream would replace this later without changing the events.

<p class="sdk-muted">From <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md">spec/operations.md</a>.</p>

</details>

<p class="sdk-see">See also: <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md#clusterwatch">spec/operations.md</a> · <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/src/cluster/index.ts#L142">source</a></p>

## Checks {#group-checks}

### cluster.verifyDefinition {#verifyDefinition}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">pure</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 1</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#create">3. Create and join the cluster</a></div>

Verifies a cluster definition before it is signed or used:

1. its `config_hash` equals `configHash` when given (case-insensitive);
2. the config hash recomputed for its `version` equals `config_hash`;
3. `fork_version` is the genesis fork version of `chainId`;
4. every signature it carries (creator, operator config hash, operator
   ENR) is valid for its signer in the EIP-712 domain of `chainId`;
   contract-wallet signers (a Safe) are checked with EIP-1271, which needs
   a client for `chainId` (`publicClients`, or `publicClient` on that
   chain): without one, a signature that does not recover to its signer
   is `signature_unverifiable`.

All issues are reported, not only the first.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.cluster.verifyDefinition(
  input: {
    definition: unknown;
    configHash?: string;
    chainId?: number;
  },
  options?: VerifyOptions,
): Promise<DefinitionVerification>
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>input</code> | <span class="sdk-type">{ definition: unknown; configHash?: string; chainId?: number }</span> |  |
| <code>input.definition</code> | <span class="sdk-type">unknown</span> |  |
| <code>input.configHash?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |
| <code>input.chainId?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">number</span> |  |
| <code>options?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/cluster#VerifyOptions">VerifyOptions</a></span> |  |
| <code>options.publicClient?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">PublicClient</span> | For signatures on its own chain only; one on another chain is ignored. |
| <code>options.publicClients?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/checks#PublicClients">PublicClients</a></span> | Clients by chain id, for a caller that checks signatures of several chains (a server). <span class="sdk-from">from <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/checks#SignatureClients">SignatureClients</a></span></span> |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">Promise&lt;<a href="./types/cluster#DefinitionVerification">DefinitionVerification</a>&gt;</span>

**Throws** <span class="sdk-muted">(per spec)</span> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--error" href="../errors#DEFINITION_INVALID">DEFINITION_INVALID</a> <span class="sdk-muted">plus the [checks every operation runs](../errors.md#checks-every-operation-runs)</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { cluster } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const check = await obol.cluster.verifyDefinition({ definition, configHash });
if (!check.ok) console.log(check.issues);
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: cluster.verifyDefinition</summary>

Tag: `pure`. Inputs: `{ definition, configHash: Hash32?, chainId: uint }`. Output: `{ ok: bool, issues: { code,
message }[] }`; `cluster.accept` throws `DEFINITION_INVALID` with these issues.

1. The definition's `config_hash` equals `configHash` when given (case-insensitive). Issue `config_hash_mismatch`.
2. Recomputed config hash equals `config_hash`. Issue `config_hash_mismatch` (or `version_unsupported`).
3. `fork_version` equals the chain's genesis fork version (`0x00000000` mainnet, `0x10000910` Hoodi, `0x00000064`
   Gnosis, `0x90000069` Sepolia). Issue `fork_version_mismatch`. (2.15)
4. For a definition with signatures: the creator and operator EIP-712 signatures as distributed-validator-specs
   "EIP-712 Signature Computation" (contract-wallet signers via EIP-1271, which makes this step `chain`). Issue
   `signature_invalid`; `signature_unverifiable` for a signature that does not recover to its signer when no client
   for `chainId` was given (see "Contract-wallet signatures" below). (2.15 `verifyDefinitionSignatures`, run only
   inside lock verification today; `new` for accept)

Options: `{ publicClient: PublicClient?, publicClients: Record&lt;chainId, PublicClient> | (chainId) => PublicClient?
}`; a `publicClients` that is neither: `PAYLOAD_INVALID`. The bound `obol.cluster.verifyDefinition` adds the client's
own `publicClient` for the client chain.

**Contract-wallet signatures.** Every signature is first recovered (ECDSA). One that does not recover to its signer is
checked as a contract wallet's (EIP-1271 `isValidSignature(bytes32 hashTypedData, signature)` returning `0x1626ba7e`,
else the legacy `isValidSignature(bytes data, signature)` returning `0x20c13b0b`, with the 32-byte hash as `data`, as
Safes before 1.3.0 implement it and 2.x accepted; each magic counts only from its own function) with the client for
the domain's chain: from `publicClients` (a client on another chain than the one it is listed for is
ignored), else `publicClient` when it is on that chain. With a client: an address with no code (or an EIP-7702
delegation) is `invalid`; a contract that refuses, reverts or fails the read is `invalid`. Without one the SDK cannot
tell an account from a contract wallet, so the signature is `unverifiable`: a failure (`ok: false`) that names the
missing client instead of passing for `invalid`. The SDK has no RPCs of its own (2.x used built-in ones,
`PROVIDER_MAP`), so a server passes `publicClients` for every chain it serves.

<p class="sdk-muted">From <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md">spec/operations.md</a>.</p>

</details>

### cluster.verifyLock {#verifyLock}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">pure (chain when a definition signer is a contract wallet: EIP-1271 call)</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 1</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#dkg">4. DKG and lock</a></div>

Verifies a cluster lock before use. Steps, in order (the first failure is
reported as `step`, with `validator` for a per-validator one):

1. the definition flow is group, solo or Charon (`definition_flow_unknown`);
2. the definition is one Charon accepts (`definition_invalid`);
3. the definition signatures the flow needs are valid
   (`definition_signature_invalid`). Contract-wallet signers (a Safe) are
   checked with EIP-1271 and **need a client for the lock's chain**
   (`publicClients`, or `publicClient` on that chain; 2.x had built-in
   RPCs, v3 has none): without one, a signature that does not recover to
   its signer is `definition_signature_unverifiable`;
4. recomputed config, definition and lock hashes equal the stored ones
   (`hash_mismatch`). `config_hash` is recomputed from the definition
   fields, so the signatures of step 3 (all over `config_hash`) bind to
   the definition's contents;
5. one public share per operator, unique group keys, no repeated share
   (`share_layout_invalid`);
6. `full`: the shares and group key of each validator lie on one
   polynomial of degree below the threshold, every share checked
   (`share_reconstruction_failed`);
7. deposit data: amounts, group pubkey, `0x01` / `0x02` credentials to the
   withdrawal address; BLS signatures for the checked validators
   (`deposit_data_invalid`);
8. builder registrations: group pubkey, fee recipient; BLS signatures for
   the checked validators (`builder_registration_invalid`; from v1.7.0);
9. node signatures by each operator's ENR key over `lock_hash` (from
   v1.7.0) and, `full`, `signature_aggregate` over `lock_hash` against all
   public shares (`lock_signature_invalid`).

`level: 'attested'` skips the BLS work of steps 6 and 9 and checks the
step 7 / 8 signatures of the validators in `signatures` only (a 10k
validator lock: a few seconds, plus about 25 ms per checked signature with
the default backend). `full` (default) checks everything. **A server that
accepts locks from users must use `full`**: `attested` skips share
binding and `signature_aggregate`. On Node, pass a native backend
(`blstBackend` from `@obolnetwork/obol-sdk/blst`) to keep `full` fast.

The result is an object, always truthy: test `result.ok`, or use
`isValidLock` for a boolean.

With `signal`, an abort stops the run at the next yield point.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.cluster.verifyLock(
  lock: unknown,
  options?: VerifyLockOptions,
): Promise<LockVerification>
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>lock</code> | <span class="sdk-type">unknown</span> |  |
| <code>options?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/cluster#VerifyLockOptions">VerifyLockOptions</a></span> |  |
| <code>options.publicClient?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">PublicClient</span> | A client for contract-wallet (EIP-1271) definition signatures, such as a Safe creator: used for a lock on its own chain only. The SDK has no RPCs of its own (2.x had built-in ones). See `publicClients`. |
| <code>options.publicClients?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/checks#PublicClients">PublicClients</a></span> | Clients by chain id (or a function of the chain id), for a caller that verifies locks of several chains: the one for the lock's chain (from its `fork_version`) checks contract-wallet signatures. Without a client for that chain, a definition signature that does not recover to its signer fails as `definition_signature_unverifiable`. |
| <code>options.level?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/cluster#LockVerificationLevel">LockVerificationLevel</a></span> | Default `full`. |
| <code>options.signatures?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">'all' &#124; 'none' &#124; number[]</span> | Validators (indexes in the lock) whose deposit and builder registration BLS signatures `attested` checks: `all`, `none` (default) or a list. `full` checks all of them (only `all` is accepted with it). |
| <code>options.yieldMs?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">number</span> | Longest stretch of work, in ms, between yields to the event loop (default 50; 0 = never yield). A stretch can overrun it by one unit of work (one signature, about 25 ms with the default backend). |
| <code>options.bls?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/checks#BlsBackend">BlsBackend</a></span> | BLS backend (default `nobleBls`, pure JavaScript). |
| <code>options.signal?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">AbortSignal</span> | Aborts the verification: checked at every yield point (between units of work), and an abort throws [`ABORTED`](../errors.md#ABORTED) with the signal's reason as `cause`. The way for a server to bound the CPU spent per request, e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)`. With `yieldMs: 0` the event loop never runs during the call, so a timer cannot fire mid-run. |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">Promise&lt;<a href="./types/cluster#LockVerification">LockVerification</a>&gt;</span>

**Throws** <span class="sdk-muted">(per spec)</span> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--error" href="../errors#ABORTED">ABORTED</a> <span class="sdk-muted">plus the [checks every operation runs](../errors.md#checks-every-operation-runs)</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { cluster } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const result = await obol.cluster.verifyLock(lock); // level 'full' by default
if (!result.ok) console.log(result.step, result.issue, result.validator);
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: cluster.verifyLock</summary>

Tag: `pure` (`chain` when a definition signer is a contract wallet: EIP-1271 call). Inputs: a lock,

```
{ level: "attested" | "full" (default "full"),
  signatures: "all" | "none" | uint[],   # attested only (default "none"): validators whose step 7 / 8 BLS signatures are checked
  yieldMs: uint (default 50),            # 0 = never yield
  signal: AbortSignal?,                  # checked at every yield point; aborted → ABORTED (cause: signal.reason)
  bls: BlsBackend?,                      # default: pure JS (@noble/curves); Node: loadBlstBackend() from /blst
  publicClient: PublicClient?,           # contract-wallet signatures on its own chain
  publicClients: Record<chainId, PublicClient> | (chainId) => PublicClient? }  # by the lock's chain
```

An options key outside this list is [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) (`unknown_key`), also through `isValidLock` (3.0.0-rc.12;
before, `{ level: "attested", signature: "all" }` silently checked no BLS signature).

A lock whose definition `version` the SDK does not implement (v1.9.0, or below v1.6.0) fails first, before any other
step, as `{ ok: false, step: "hash_mismatch", issue: "version_unsupported" }` (3.0.0-rc.12 reports it first; a
v1.9.0 lock used to fail at whichever earlier step its contents tripped). v1.9.0 is not supported by design: the
Obol API does not accept it.

Output: `{ ok: bool, level, step: string?, issue: string?, validator: uint? }`; `validator` is the index of the
failing validator when the failing check is per validator (steps 5–8). Steps: `definition_flow_unknown`,
`definition_invalid`, `definition_signature_invalid`, `definition_signature_unverifiable`, `hash_mismatch`,
`share_layout_invalid`,
`share_reconstruction_failed`, `deposit_data_invalid`, `builder_registration_invalid`, `lock_signature_invalid`.

The full "Verifying a Lock Before Use" sequence of distributed-validator-specs, plus the Obol definition and deposit
rules, in this order (first failure is reported as `step`):

1. Definition flow is one of: group (creator and every operator signed), solo (creator signed, operators carry only
   ENRs), Charon (nothing signed). Else `definition_flow_unknown`. (2.15 `definitionFlow`)
2. What Charon refuses when it loads the definition, for every flow: a `fork_version` of no chain in the table
   (`fork_version_unknown`); `num_validators` other than the number of `validators` (`num_validators_mismatch`); for
   v1.8.0+, a non-empty `deposit_amounts` with an amount below 1 ETH or above 32 ETH (2048 ETH with `compounding`), or
   summing to less than 32 ETH (`deposit_amounts_invalid`). `definition_invalid`. (new in 3.0.0-rc.4, from the
   differential fuzz against Charon)
3. Definition signatures valid for the flow (as `verifyDefinition` 4, with the lock's chain from its
   `fork_version`). `definition_signature_invalid` for a signature known to be invalid (reported first, if any);
   else `definition_signature_unverifiable` for one that could not be checked: it does not recover to its signer and
   no client for the lock's chain was given (see `verifyDefinition` "Contract-wallet signatures"). The issue names
   the signature (`creator config_signature`, `operators[i] enr_signature`, ...). (`definition_signature_unverifiable`
   new in 3.0.0-rc.5; rc.4 reported it as `definition_signature_invalid`)
4. Recomputed `config_hash`, `definition_hash` and `lock_hash` equal the stored values. `hash_mismatch`, issue
   `config_hash`, `definition_hash` or `lock_hash` (the first that differs). (spec step 1) `config_hash` is
   recomputed from the definition's fields, never taken as given: the creator and operator signatures of step 3 are
   over `config_hash`, so this is what binds them to the definition's contents. An edited definition with its old
   `config_hash` passes step 3 and fails here (`config_hash`), however `definition_hash`, `lock_hash` and the node
   signatures were re-sealed; one with `config_hash` recomputed fails step 3 (the signatures are over the old hash);
   and a self-consistent lock that carries another cluster's `config_hash` fails here too.
5. Every validator has exactly one public share per operator, no two validators share a group key, no validator
   repeats a share (case-insensitive). `share_layout_invalid`. (spec step 2)
6. `full`: the shares bind to the group key. With Y0 the group key and Yj the share at index j (1-based, file order),
   the points Y0 … Yn lie on one polynomial of degree below `threshold`: every `threshold`-th forward difference is
   the identity. This accepts exactly what "recover from the first `threshold`, then once per remaining share
   substituted in" accepts. Y0 … Y(threshold-1) are checked to be in the prime-order subgroup; the later points are
   then integer combinations of them. No point may be the identity. `share_reconstruction_failed` (issue
   `malformed_share` for a point that does not decode). (spec step 3)
7. Deposit amounts as Charon's DKG makes them: v1.6.0 / v1.7.0 one 32 ETH deposit; v1.8.0+ every amount of
   `deposit_amounts` in each validator's `partial_deposit_data` (`deposit_amount_missing`) and no other amount
   (`deposit_amount_unexpected`), where an empty `deposit_amounts` allows Charon's defaults (1 and 32 ETH; 1, 8, 32
   and 256 ETH with `compounding`) without requiring them (earlier Charon releases made the 32 ETH deposit only).
   Each deposit has the validator's group pubkey, credentials `0x01` (or `0x02` with `compounding`, a v1.10.0+ field;
   v1.8.0 has no `compounding` and is never read as compounding) + 11 zero bytes + the validator's withdrawal address
   (issues `deposit_data_missing`, `deposit_fields`, every validator);
   then, for the checked validators (all with `full`), a valid BLS signature in the deposit domain of the fork
   (`signature_invalid`). `deposit_data_invalid`. (2.15)
8. Each builder registration has the group pubkey and the definition's fee recipient (`builder_registration_fields`,
   every validator), and, for the checked validators, a valid signature in the builder domain (`signature_invalid`).
   `builder_registration_invalid`. (2.15; distributed-validator-specs leaves it out of scope)
9. One node signature per operator, each exactly 65 bytes `r ‖ s ‖ v` with `v` in {0, 1, 27, 28}, and the key
   recovered from it over `lock_hash` with that recovery id is the operator's ENR key (as Charon `k1util.Verify65`:
   the high-s form is accepted, a 64-byte signature or a wrong recovery id is not);
   `full`: `signature_aggregate` verifies over `lock_hash` against the sum of all public shares (plain aggregate).
   `lock_signature_invalid`. (spec step 4)

Levels. `full` runs everything. `attested` runs the steps that need no BLS work (1–5, the field checks of 7 and 8,
the node signatures of 9) plus the step 7 / 8 signatures of the validators in `signatures`. Charon verifies every
deposit and builder signature during the DKG before each node signs `lock_hash`, so valid node signatures over a
matching `lock_hash` attest to them; a depositor still checks the signatures of the deposits it sends.
`level: "full"` with `signatures` other than `"all"`, or an index outside the lock: [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID).

Point encodings are checked to be canonical before they are decoded (ZCash compressed format, as Ethereum
`KeyValidate` and blst): the compression flag set; the infinity flag only with every other bit zero; each field
element (G1 `x`; G2 `x.c1` and `x.c0`) below the field modulus, since `x + p` would decode to the same point. A
non-canonical public share, group key or signature fails its step (`malformed_share`, `signature_invalid`). (new in
3.0.0-rc.4)

BLS signature checks (steps 7, 8 and [`deposits.assertDepositData`](./deposits.md#assertDepositData)) run in batches of 32: each signature is weighted
by a fresh secret random 64-bit scalar and every point is checked to be in the prime-order subgroup and not the
identity, so a batch passes only if every signature in it is valid on its own (a plain sum would accept invalid
signatures that cancel out). A failing batch is checked one signature at a time, and the first invalid one is
reported.

Everything runs on the calling thread, with no workers and no time limit: the work yields to the event loop at
least every `yieldMs` (it yields once half of it has passed, and one signature is about 25 ms of pure JS work), so a
caller stays responsive. A caller that needs a deadline passes `signal` (`AbortSignal.timeout(ms)`, or a request's
own signal): it is checked before the run and at every yield point, and once aborted the run stops there with
[`ABORTED`](../errors.md#ABORTED) (details `operation`, `cause` the signal's `reason`), so a server bounds the CPU it spends per request
(racing the promise would leave the work running). An already-aborted signal throws before any work; a value that is
not an `AbortSignal` is [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID). With `yieldMs: 0` nothing yields, so a timer-based signal cannot fire
mid-run. Cost, measured on one thread
(Node 24) with synthetic locks of 3 signatures per validator: with the default backend, 1k validators `full` about
80 s (signatures about 25 ms each; share binding 5 s) and `attested` 0.3 s, 10k validators `attested` 1.8 s; with
an adapter over `@chainsafe/blst` (see the TSDoc of [`BlsBackend`](./types/checks.md#BlsBackend)), `full` 1.3 s for 1k and 12 s for 10k.

Servers. `full` is the level for locks from users: `attested` skips share binding and `signature_aggregate`. With
the default backend a 1k-validator lock is about 80 s of event-loop time; a Node server passes the native backend
(below). The result is an object (always truthy): test `ok`, or use `isValidLock`.

Vectors: the `cluster_hashing.json` hash cases. (`real_keys_3_of_4`, a Sepolia lock, has placeholder EIP-712,
deposit and builder signatures, so it stops at its creator signature: `definition_signature_unverifiable` without a
Sepolia client; it is not a full-pass fixture.)

</details>

### cluster.isValidLock {#isValidLock}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">pure (chain as verifyLock)</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 1</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#dkg">4. DKG and lock</a></div>

isValidLock (pure; `chain` for a contract-wallet signer): `verifyLock` as
a boolean, the drop-in for the 2.x `validateClusterLock`. Runs at
`level: 'full'` unless `options.level` says otherwise (a server that
accepts locks must keep `full`), with the other options passed through
(`bls`, `publicClient` / `publicClients`, `yieldMs`, `signal`). A
malformed lock ([`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID)) is `false`, as in 2.x; any other error
is thrown, including [`ABORTED`](../errors.md#ABORTED) from `signal` (never `false`).

```ts sdk-signature

  lock: unknown,
  options?: VerifyLockOptions,
): Promise<boolean>
```

**Example**

```ts

const valid = await obol.cluster.isValidLock(lock); // false, never a throw, for a bad lock
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: cluster.isValidLock</summary>

Tag: `pure` (`chain` as `verifyLock`). Inputs: a lock, the `verifyLock` options. Output: `bool`. The 2.x
`validateClusterLock`. Runs `verifyLock` with `level: "full"` unless `options.level` is given, and returns `ok`. A
[`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) for the lock (a malformed lock; issue paths under `lock`) is `false`, as 2.x returned; one for the
options (paths under `options`) and every other error are thrown, including [`ABORTED`](../errors.md#ABORTED) from `signal` (an abort is
never `false`). Also a root export and bound
(`obol.cluster.isValidLock`, with the client's `publicClient` for its chain). (new in 3.0.0-rc.5)

<p class="sdk-muted">From <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md">spec/operations.md</a>.</p>

</details>

<p class="sdk-see">See also: <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md#clusterisvalidlock">spec/operations.md</a> · <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/src/cluster/index.ts#L154">source</a></p>

### cluster.isValidEnr {#isValidEnr}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">pure</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--pure" title="Exported from the namespace, not bound on the client">namespace only</span></div>

isValidEnr (pure): whether `enr` is a validly signed text ENR (`enr:-…`).
Never throws. Whitespace is not trimmed: a record with surrounding
whitespace is not valid.

```ts sdk-signature
cluster.isValidEnr(enr: unknown): boolean
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>enr</code> | <span class="sdk-type">unknown</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">boolean</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { cluster } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const enrOk = cluster.isValidEnr(enr);
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: cluster.parseEnr / cluster.isValidEnr (shared section)</summary>

Tag: `pure`. `parseEnr(enr)`: decodes a text ENR (`enr:` + base64url RLP, EIP-778) and checks its signature, as 2.x
`ENR.decodeTxt`; output `{ publicKey: Hex (33-byte compressed secp256k1), nodeId: Hex, seq: bigint, ip?, tcp?, udp?
}`; anything else: `PAYLOAD_INVALID` (path `enr`). `isValidEnr(value)`: `true` iff `parseEnr` would succeed; never
throws; whitespace is not trimmed. (new in 3.0.0-rc.5; 2.x re-exported the `@chainsafe/enr` class)

<p class="sdk-muted">From <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md">spec/operations.md</a>.</p>

</details>

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--pure" title="Exported from the namespace, not bound on the client">namespace only</span></div>

`CreatorConfigHash { creator_config_hash }`, signed by the creator.

```ts sdk-signature
cluster.creatorConfigHashTypedData(
  configHash: string,
  chainId: number,
): ClusterTypedData
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

|---|---|---|
| <code>configHash</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |
| <code>chainId</code> | <span class="sdk-type">number</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">ClusterTypedData</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { cluster } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';
import { createWalletClient, custom } from 'viem';
import { hoodi } from 'viem/chains';

// The EIP-712 payloads the SDK signs, for signing with your own wallet layer.
const wallet = createWalletClient({ account, chain: hoodi, transport: custom(window.ethereum!) });
const creatorSig = await wallet.signTypedData(cluster.creatorConfigHashTypedData(configHash, 560048));
```

## Constants {#group-constants}

### cluster.nobleBls {#nobleBls}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--pure" title="Exported from the namespace, not bound on the client">namespace only</span></div>

The default backend: pure JavaScript on `@noble/curves`, in Node and in
browsers. Batches use random 64-bit weights; points that are not
subgroup-checked are decoded with one square root.

```ts sdk-signature
cluster.nobleBls: BlsBackend
```
